articles.title: AR Rahman praises Kashmir as ‘beautiful’ and ‘blessed’, urges filmmakers to focus on nature instead of violence
articles.summary: Oscar-winning composer AR Rahman has spoken about Kashmir’s immense potential as a destination for filmmakers, musicians and artists, describing the V.
articles.body: Oscar-winning composer AR Rahman has spoken about Kashmir’s immense potential as a destination for filmmakers, musicians and artists, describing the Valley as a “beautiful” and “blessed” place. During his visit, Rahman also backed the International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir and expressed hope that the event grows into a globally recognised platform.The composer believes that showcasing Kashmir’s natural beauty, culture and hospitality through cinema could help create a fresh perception of the region. He also encouraged Bollywood filmmakers to explore the Valley while working more closely with local musicians and folk artistes.A R Rahman praises Kashmir as a filmmaking destinationSpeaking to ANI, Rahman said the region’s atmosphere and scenic surroundings make it particularly suited for creative pursuits. He also praised the idea of hosting an international film festival in Kashmir, saying it could give audiences from across the world an opportunity to experience the Valley.“Kashmir is a beautiful place and it’s blessed. So having an international film festival is commendable and everybody can see the beauty of Kashmir and the vibration of Kashmir. I wish this film festival becomes really famous and a lot of people come here and enjoy the hospitality of the Kashmiri people," he said.Rahman also revealed that his ongoing visit to Kashmir was connected to an advertising project. “I’ve come for an ad. I’ll tell you what it is. We enjoyed shooting the ad, we just finished it," he said.Composer hints at returning for a performanceRahman further indicated that his association with Kashmir could extend beyond his current project. He said discussions are underway for possible future plans, including a live performance in the Valley.“Yes, we have some plans, and we are talking. Hopefully, I want to come and perform here," he said.A R Rahman wants Bollywood to focus on Kashmir's beautyWhen asked whether Bollywood should shoot more films in Kashmir, Rahman agreed that filmmakers should present the region through its natural beauty and peaceful surroundings instead of repeatedly associating it with violence and its troubled past.“That’s a very good point. I think that’s what should happen from now. They should bring the beauty and the peace when you see nature as a positive thing rather than talking about violence or the past. The past is past, and the future is bright," he said.He recalls working with Kashmiri folk singers on RockstarRahman also highlighted the contribution of local artistes and folk music, recalling his own experience of recording Kashmiri singers for ‘Rockstar’.“I think that’s a beautiful suggestion and I would love to. I came here for ‘Rockstar’. I recorded the ladies singing folk songs, and we used it in Rockstar. We want to come and do more things here. We want to come and do more things here," he said.For Rahman, greater collaboration between Bollywood and Kashmiri musicians could open up opportunities to bring the region’s traditional sounds to wider audiences.Rahman hopes Kashmir festival reaches global statureSpeaking about the International Film Festival of Jammu and Kashmir, the composer said its current beginning could eventually lead to a major international platform. He cited prominent film festivals around the world while expressing his wish to see Kashmir establish itself among India's leading cinematic events.“Yes, this is a great opening. I wish it will grow and grow and become such a great experience. We go to Amsterdam, and we go to London Film Festival and Sundance. I wish Kashmir becomes the best festival in India," he added.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. Download the TOI app.Give your child the gift of confidence! articles.title: York bookshop owner becomes character in Janice Hallett novel
articles.summary: A bookshop owner from York has won a competition to have a character named after her in a new book.
articles.body:
As the owner of a bookshop specialising in "whodunnits", Isla Coole is no stranger to the world of crime fiction.

Now, she is at the heart of a murder mystery story herself after she won a competition to have a character named after her in the latest book by bestselling author Janice Hallett, The Silent Appeal.

The 46-year-old opened her York shop, Criminally Good Books, on Colliergate in 2024.

"People have been excitedly waiting for this book, so I'm super chuffed to be in it," says Isla.

The opportunity came about when Isla attended the Theakston Old Peculier Crime Writing Festival in Harrogate, where Hallett was a guest.

"There was a competition to get your name, or a loved one's name, featured in a future book of Janice's - where you had to guess how many boiled sweets are in this massive jar," says Isla.

"I know a lot about sweets and I guessed the closest and got a lovely message about a month later saying congratulations you've won, and we'll be in touch with you to let you know what book you'll be in."

In Hallett's previous book, The Appeal, readers followed two paralegals called Femi and Charlotte, who were tasked by their boss to go through the correspondence of an amateur dramatics society to try and figure out why their client confessed to a murder that they didn't commit.

The reader does not know who their client is until close to the end - or what it is they are supposed to have done.

The Silent Appeal revisits the group as they prepare to stage another production.

Megan Ponting, 37, who works for Criminally Good Books, says Isla's character is "quite significant to the plot".

"You always kind of hope that you would have a big role and so I was just really excited when I found out," adds Isla.

Hallett was originally a screenwriter, but began writing crime novels following a suggestion from her agent.

She now has an army of fans who love her unusual style.

"The books are not written like traditional novels, and you have to almost solve the puzzle along with the cast of characters," says Isla.

"It's really interesting, and an unusual way of writing and reading a book, because you're reading emails, text messages and posters - and even post-it notes."

Hallett, who will promote the book at Isla's shop on Wednesday, reveals Isla gave her free rein to get creative with her character.

"I was writing The Silent Appeal and asked Isla if she had any objection to being a 'bad' character, because I never know when I create a character whether they will end up committing a terrible crime or even being murdered themselves.

"The Isla Coole in The Silent Appeal is a Canadian stand-up comedian with a vital piece of the murder mystery puzzle."

Addressing her upcoming event, she adds: "It's the first time one of my characters has booked me for a public appearance!"

Isla believes the ongoing appeal of what is known as the "cosy crime" genre has played a big part in the success of her shop, which Hallett said was "famous" within the crime writers' community.

"People just love putting themselves in the position of the amateur detective to see if they can solve the mystery," she says.

"Some people like to be scared, some people like to solve a puzzle, some people like to learn about another place and time.

"For a lot of people, it's kind of an escape, but without being too out there."

There has also been a rise in interest in the horror genre, and Isla is currently refurbishing what will be her second store in the city centre, which opens in October.

"This one hopefully will be really successful. We announced that we were doing this like two weeks ago and we've had over 75,000 people just view the post saying we're opening up another shop.

"We're really grateful, and hopefully that's a good indication of how interested people are in specialist bookshops."

articles.body: A Facebook post by Marathi actor Vikas Samudre threw the Mumbai Cyber Police into a state of alarm on Friday night, after a typographical slip in the message appeared to suggest he was contemplating suicide. The error triggered an urgent search operation, which continued until the confusion was finally resolved.What Vikas Samudre wrote on social mediaTaking to his social media, Vikas wrote, “I m comiting suicide... अशी माझी पोस्ट टायपिंग errors मुळे झाली...I m doing drama अशी पोस्ट करायची होती मला...काळजी.नसावी.. मी सुरक्षित आहे...Thanks for ur love”. (I am committing suicide... Aashi majhi post jaali due to typing errors...I m doing drama Aashi post karni hoti mala...Kalji.Nasavi.. I am safe...Thanks for ur love)Vikas Samudre clarifies the confusionSamudre subsequently confirmed that he was fine, explaining that the post was actually tied to a theatre project he was working on. The message had spread rapidly online, drawing concerned calls from the Mumbai Commissioner of Police as well as several other top officials.How police traced Vikas SamudreStarting at 11.03 pm, the cyber lab along with five cyber officers and control room staff worked to trace Samudre's location, eventually reaching him by 12.15 am.Vikas Samudre's career in Marathi entertainmentVikas Samudre has carved a niche for himself across both Marathi theatre and cinema, taking on a variety of roles over the years. Audiences have particularly warmed to his comic performances, and it was the film 'Navra Maza Navsacha' that brought him widespread recognition. His natural, effortless acting style has helped him build a unique identity within the Marathi entertainment industry.A typo in Marathi actor Vikas Samudre's Facebook post appeared to suggest suicidal intent, alarming Mumbai Cyber Police on Friday night. A team traced him within an hour. Samudre clarified he was safe and the post related to a drama project. articles.body: Akshay Kumar's journey in Bollywood has included an unexpected connection with one of Hindi cinema's biggest stars, Rajesh Khanna. Before becoming his son-in-law, Akshay Kumar had approached the veteran actor while looking for work.In an old interview with Filmy New, Akshay Kumar remembered a time when he would visit Rajesh Khanna's office with his photographs. He hoped the superstar might consider him for a film. At that stage, marriage into the Khanna family was something he could never have imagined. “There are so many things that have happened in my life that I never thought off. Meine zindagi mein nahi socha tha ki mein Rajesh Khanna ki beti se shaadi karunga. Kabhi bhi nahi socha tha (I never imagined that I would marry Rajesh Khanna’s daughter). Mein unke office mein jaya karta tha apni photo le ke ki mujhe koi kaam de do. Woh bolte they theek hai baad mein aana abhi film bana raha hun (I used to go to his office with my photograph, asking for work. He used to tell me to come later).”He eventually became Rajesh Khanna's son-in-lawAkshay Kumar's professional pursuit of Rajesh Khanna eventually gained a remarkable personal connection. He later fell in love with Twinkle Khanna, the superstar's daughter. The couple got married in 2001 and went on to build a family together. The actor's recollection therefore carries a sense of irony. The aspiring performer who once entered Rajesh Khanna's office seeking an opportunity eventually became part of his family. Akshay Kumar has previously spoken about how dramatically his circumstances changed over the years. His memories of Rajesh Khanna also extend beyond their relationship as actor and son-in-law.Akshay Kumar remembers Rajesh Khanna's adviceDuring a recent appearance at the India Today Conclave, Akshay Kumar discussed what he learned from Rajesh Khanna. Rather than describing only the veteran actor's achievements, he spoke about the lessons that came from his experiences. “I have learned a lot from my father-in-law. What did I learn from him? I learned what not to do. That’s actually the truth.” Akshay Kumar also recalled how openly Rajesh Khanna discussed his own career with him. According to the actor, his father-in-law spoke about the mistakes he had made during his extraordinary journey. “He honestly sat down with me and used to tell me about the mistakes he had made. He was the number one superstar; India has seen that.”He remembered seeing Rajesh Khanna as a childAkshay Kumar's association with Rajesh Khanna began even before they became relatives. The actor has recalled seeing the superstar's influence during his childhood. As a young boy, Akshay Kumar would pass Rajesh Khanna's Mumbai home, Aashirwad, with his parents. The residence was one of the places where fans gathered in the hope of catching a glimpse of the immensely popular actor. Akshay Kumar remembered waiting outside the bungalow for an opportunity to see Rajesh Khanna. Years later, his own life brought him much closer to the same star. Rajesh Khanna died on July 18, 2012, at the age of 69. He passed away at his Mumbai residence, Aashirwad, after reportedly battling cancer.Akshay Kumar remains active across multiple genres and continues to headline major Hindi film projects. His recent release is 'Haiwaan', directed by Priyadarshan. articles.title: When Farah Khan revealed why Shilpa Shirodkar didn’t bag ‘Chaiyya Chaiyya’ with Shah Rukh Khan: ‘She was 100 kg, where would he stand?’
articles.summary: ‘Chhaiya Chhaiya’ remains one of the most iconic songs in Hindi cinema, but the face associated with the track could have been very different. Before .
articles.body: ‘Chhaiya Chhaiya’ remains one of the most iconic songs in Hindi cinema, but the face associated with the track could have been very different. Before Malaika Arora became synonymous with the song, Farah Khan had considered Shilpa Shirodkar for the memorable dance number from Mani Ratnam’s ‘Dil Se’. Years later, Farah opened up about the casting process and recalled why Shirodkar did not eventually feature in the song. Her explanation centred on the practical challenges of filming a demanding dance sequence on top of a moving train.Shilpa Shirodkar was considered for the iconic songFarah, who choreographed ‘Chhaiya Chhaiya’, revisited the casting story during a conversation with Karanveer Mehra on her YouTube channel. She revealed that Shilpa was among the actresses she had approached for the song.“I came to Shilpa to ask her for ‘Chhaiya Chhaiya.’ But something must have happened to her because at that time, she was at least 100 kgs. So I thought, ‘How will she get on the train? And if she gets on, where will Shah Rukh stand?’”The sequence required the female performer to dance alongside Shah Rukh Khan on top of a moving train, making physical movement and space important considerations during the shoot.Raveena Tandon and Shilpa Shetty also turned it downShilpa Shirodkar was not the only actress considered before Malaika Arora eventually landed the part. Farah had also approached Raveena Tandon and Shilpa Shetty, but both reportedly declined the opportunity for personal reasons.The role ultimately went to Malaika, whose energetic performance alongside Shah Rukh became one of the defining visuals of ‘Dil Se’. The song went on to achieve cult status and remains one of the most remembered dance numbers of the 1990s.Shilpa later spoke about losing the opportunityShilpa Shirodkar herself addressed the episode during an interview with Siddharth Kannan. She confirmed that she had been approached for ‘Chhaiya Chhaiya’ but believed her weight ultimately became the reason she was not selected.“I didn’t get it because I was fat. They just said that I am fat,” she recalled.Although missing the song was understandably disappointing, Shilpa said she chose to look at her career beyond that one opportunity.“I will always feel bad that I didn’t get ‘Chhaiya Chhaiya,’ but God gave me much more, and He is still giving me.”She no longer remembers exactly what Farah told herShilpa also remembered the conversation she had with Farah at the time, although she admitted that the details had faded over the years.“She just said that we will work some other time because they are looking for someone else. ‘You are a little fatter.’ Something like this… I don’t even remember anymore. I know I missed it because I was fat.”Shilpa continued to build a successful careerMissing out on one of Bollywood’s most iconic songs did not stop Shilpa from carving out a successful career. She went on to appear in films including ‘Hum’, ‘Gopi Kishan’ and ‘Aankhein’.Decades later, she found herself back in the spotlight with her participation in ‘Bigg Boss 18’. Her stint on the reality show introduced her to a newer generation of viewers, while her candid personality and resilience earned her appreciation during her time inside the house.Although she did not win the reality show, Shilpa’s journey added another chapter to a career that had already spanned several decades.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Zachary Levi calls California a ‘failed state’ that is ‘literally and figuratively on fire’ after Texas move
articles.summary: Zachary Levi calls California a "failed state" after leaving Hollywood for Texas. The 'Chuck' actor is starring in Guy Moshe's new action-thriller 'The Fix' opposite Liam Neeson.
articles.body: Zachary Levi isn't holding back about why he packed up and left his home state of California for Texas. In 2017, the 45-year-old actor, who is starring in the upcoming action-thriller "The Fix," sold his home in Los Angeles and bought a ranch outside of Austin. During a recent interview with Fox News Digital alongside his "The Fix" co-star Liam Neeson, Levi candidly opened up about why he left the Golden State. KIRK CAMERON PRAISES NASHVILLE'S 'GOOD VALUES' AFTER DITCHING CALIFORNIA OVER COST OF LIVING, POLITICS "I grew up in California, I love California, it is a failed state," he said. "It is literally and figuratively on fire." Along with his disillusionment with California, the "Chuck" star explained that his departure was rooted in a long-standing desire to rethink how the entertainment industry operates from the inside out. NEWSOM SAYS FILM TAX INCENTIVES ARE BRINGING HOLLYWOOD HOME BUT INDUSTRY EXPERTS WARN IT MAY BE 'TOO LATE' "Ever since I started working in Hollywood and I saw how broken it all was, I felt very compelled by God to go build a better Hollywood — like a new United Artists kind of studio — where it's owned and operated by the artists, where we can cut out all the middlemen, where we all can do really well, build a community," Levi said. "And then not just a place to work," he continued. "People can live there and kids can go to school there and we have an organic farm and like all of the things that I think everybody really wants these days." WATCH: Zachary Levi calls California a 'failed state' after moving to Texas 'FRIDAY NIGHT LIGHTS' STAR ADRIANNE PALICKI SAYS TEXAS GAVE HER SOMETHING HOLLYWOOD COULDN'T "We look at the regular world around us and we see it burning and we're like, 'Can we do this better? I feel like we can do this better," Levi added. "So that all culminated in nine years ago, me finding 75 acres outside of Austin, Texas to buy, to develop, to turn into this magical kind of idea. That's why I left." Levi is fulfilling his vision by building Wyldwood Studios, a $100 million film and lifestyle campus on his 75-acre property in Bastrop County outside Austin. PARAMOUNT ESCALATES THREAT TO LEAVE CALIFORNIA AS DEM AG'S ANTITRUST LAWSUIT STALLS WARNER BROS MERGER Designed as a hybrid production hub and creative retreat, the multi-phase project pairs soundstages and production offices with residential housing and wellness spaces. Wyldwood is expected to open its first two soundstages in 2027. Looking back on his decision to move, Levi explained that walking away from his life in California meant trading idyllic weather and close personal ties for a bigger mission. ‘DUCK DYNASTY’ STARS JEP AND JESSICA ROBERTSON SAY ‘A LOT OF PRAYER’ LED THEM TO LEAVE LOUISIANA FOR TEXAS "I left behind a lot of community and family and perfect weather in Southern California, but when you weigh it all out and you must, you have to come to these points in your life and you go, 'Is all of that really worth the thing that I know I'm supposed to go build in the future to make a better world?' And to me, that calling on my life was more important," he said. "Fortunately, Austin's awesome. It's great, you know?" Levi continued. "It can get kinda hot in the summer and kinda cold in the wintertime, but I can deal with it." "There's no thing as bad weather, just the wrong clothing," he added. "The Fix" marks a sharp departure for Levi, who is best known for starring in lighter projects like the action-comedy series "Chuck" and the superhero film franchise "Shazam!" TAYLOR SHERIDAN TAKES SWIPE AT LOS ANGELES AFTER BUILDING TV EMPIRE FROM TEXAS Directed by Guy Moshe, the movie follows a group of war-torn, disgraced former CIA operatives, led by Tucker (Levi) and mentored by his long-time lead Larry (Neeson), who are left disillusioned in the chaotic wake of the 2021 U.S. military withdrawal from Afghanistan. After a high-stakes mission goes disastrously wrong, the team embarks on a rogue, high-risk mission in Tehran. Seeking both a life-changing score and a chance at personal redemption, the group attempts to pull off a daring rescue operation while confronting their own past choices. TAYLOR SHERIDAN'S $330M FOUR SIXES RANCH PURCHASE FORCED HIM OUT OF RETIREMENT PLANS While speaking with Fox News Digital, Levi explained that he was drawn to the project because he wanted to take on a different character type than those that he had previously played. "I wanted to do something fun, gritty, darker, in comparison to other roles that I've played in the past, and this gave me that and then some, because there was all of the great spycraft and twists and turns and revelations throughout the story, as well as this human foundation," he said. Levi continued, "'Who are these people in real life? Why are they doing the things that they're doing? What is this redemption that they are trying to seek?' The moral ambiguity of all of that, of like, who's really the good guy and who's the bad guy. I think these are really cool themes to explore. And I got to do them with the Liam Neeson." While speaking with Fox News Digital, Neeson also explained why he joined the movie's cast, heaped praise on Levi along with Moshe, who co-wrote the screenplay with Mark Bacci. "It is a terrific script," he said. "Really, really good, talented director and writer." "He's a wonderful actor," Neeson added of Levi. "I'm not just saying that because he's here, but he is wonderful." Along with Levi and Neeson, "The Fix" also stars Annet Mahendru, Grant Harvey, Augusto Aguilera, Elnaaz Norouzi and Wes Chatham. During an interview with Fox News Digital, Moshe explained that he believed from the outset that Levi was a natural fit for the project and wasn't surprised by how hard the actor pushed himself physically for the role. "When I met him, I immediately asked myself, ‘How am I the first one to see what a great action star this guy can be?’ Like a 6'4, handsome, commanding, almost like old movie star type of kind of presence," Moshe said. "But to me with Zach, the nice thing about him is which people, I think, don't know as much about him — he's a very much of an outdoors person," he continued. "He lives in Austin, Texas on the ranch. He likes rafting. He likes to be outside. He likes to hike. I mean, he's a very physical person in real life." WATCH: ‘The Fix’ director Guy Moshe says Hollywood overlooked Zachary Levi as an action star "And he embraced it and was every bit a collaborator from day one," Moshe added. "So I wouldn't say surprised but rather validated, maybe is the word that I could use. Like I believed that this would be the case when I met him and he clearly exceeded my expectations even here." Moshe told Fox News Digital that Levi brought a raw, real-world edge to the set that surprised even the filmmakers. "Let's just say I found myself in the streets of Tbilisi in a fist fight with Zach and I throwing punches, with people in the middle of the street, which is maybe not something I should advertise," Moshe said. "But I don't know if people would expect that of him. But like he's quite a man's man in that capacity." "He's done all these movies where it's like the four-quadrant family films, all that kind of stuff, whatever, but he's certainly, I think, a much more intense person in real life in certain ways that people might not be familiar with," the director added. Norouzi also praised Levi during her interview with Fox News Digital. In "The Fix," the Iranian-born German actress plays Zara, a woman recruited to pose as the Persian wife of Tucker to help cover his cover story as a businessman while his team executes their high-stakes mission in Tehran. During the course of the movie, Zara and Tucker develop an emotional and romantic relationship amid the surrounding danger. The former "The Traitors" contestant went on to say that Levi was an "awesome" screen partner. articles.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother will make you forget all about Marvel’s Blade disaster
articles.summary: TIFF 2026 included films like Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother, In Alaska, The Face of Horror, Babies, and Drifter.
articles.body: Marvel’s mishandling of its Blade reboot will likely go down as one of the studio’s biggest mistakes. There was a great actor in place to play the vampire hunter (Mahershala Ali), and a promising director set to take over the reins (Bassam Tariq). In retrospect, though, the disappointing demise of Blade might not be such a bad thing, because Tariq and Ali have collaborated on something much more interesting than a superhero reboot: the powerful hitman thriller Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother. That was one of five movies I was able to cram into a very hectic third day at the Toronto International Film Festival (you can see my previous reports here and here), and it was one of those days that drives home why events like TIFF can be so special. Each film I saw was drastically different from the last — there was everything from a drama about drifting cars to a throwback horror flick based on a famous Japanese ghost story — which was a great reminder that there are still plenty of new ideas left in the world of film. So let’s get to it. Here are some rapid-fire reviews of everything I saw on day 3 at TIFF. [Media: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother In theaters in October Latif (Ali) lives a life of contradictions: he’s a devout Muslim and loyal father, but he also works as a hitman, albeit one who works under a specific moral code (only kill bad guys; never use a gun). But both his faith and his code are tested when his wife dies and he’s forced to become a single father to three kids, including a newborn baby. At the same time, his blood-soaked past comes back to haunt him, putting everyone at risk. We’re in a great moment for pure action flicks like Furious or the John Wick franchise, but Your Mother offers something very different. It’s a powerful character study, one where the action is comparatively fleeting, but all the more powerful and impactful because of it. It’s a film that always left me guessing just how Latif was going to get through this, and, despite being very serious and often solemn, the story also has plenty of laugh-out-loud moments. Ali is excellent as the morally questionable righteous killer, but I was also really impressed by John Cho as the villain, a charismatically unhinged leader of a right-wing church group. [Media: In Alaska No theatrical date yet A slow-burning crime thriller, In Alaska, co-directed by Jaap van Heusden and Vinnie Karetak., follows a suicidal teen named Woody (Leo Matthew Temela) who, after a tragic mishap, finds himself wanted by the FBI for causing millions of dollars worth of damage to an oil pipeline. It’s a film of two sides: Woody’s desperate attempts at survival, and veteran agent Susan (Noomi Rapace), the only who realizes the damage wasn’t caused by eco-terrorists. In Alaska is a moodier take on the genre, and one that asks some difficult and important questions about both its leads, particularly Woody, who constantly grapples with whether he even wants to live at all. What starts out bleak ends on a much more hopeful note. [Image: The Face of Horror No theatrical date yet Conceptually, Anna Biller’s The Face of Horror is a mishmash of styles and influences. It’s based on the influential Japanese ghost story Yotsuya Kaidan, but adapts the tale for 14th century England. It then renders the whole thing in the style of Technicolor horror classics. That curious combination works, though, as the film has a campy sense of theatricality to it, with over-the-top performances and classic-style special effects — including some truly memorable make-up work — that lend its grisly tale of murder and betrayal a distinct vibe. And it’s all held together by two strong lead performances: Eleanor (Kristine Froseth), the jilted wife-turned-nightmare of Edward (Jonah Hauer-King), a smarmy and morally-dubious knight who is the kind of asshole you can’t wait to see get what’s coming to him. [Image: Babies No theatrical date yet A film that explores that nagging question many long-term couples are forced to answer repeatedly: when are you going to have a baby? Written and directed by Lauren Miller Rogen, Babies is centered on Annie (Anna Kendrick) and Aaron (Seth Rogen), the only childless couple in their social circle. But Annie can’t stop thinking about the question — there’s a lot of her internal monologue debating the pros and cons of having kids — and the couple are forced to really confront the idea when a close friend and her young daughter come to stay with them, providing a taste of parenthood. Babies works for two reasons. First, it’s hilarious: Kendrick and Rogen have a blast together, and the supporting cast includes the likes of Issa Rae, Zach Cherry, and Ed Helm. But it also feels grounded in a way that makes it very relatable, whether you have kids or not. [Media: Drifter No theatrical date yet If Good Will Hunting and The Fast and the Furious were smushed together, you might get something like Drifter. The film is directed by longtime Fast star Sung Kang, who also plays the lead role of Tree, the janitor of a smalltown race track who moonlights as a driver for a drug kingpin. But all he really wants to do is drift, and events conspire to bring him to an event where he’ll go up against the best drifters in the world. The challenges are much more than just on the track, though; Tree has spent most of his life alone, so he’s forced to learn to open up to others, and he also has to contend with extracting himself from the world of crime. Unfortunately, Drifter leans too heavily on the established formula of underdog sports stories, which makes most of its beats feel predictable, with the exception of its completely improbable ending. Worse still is that, with the exception of Tree, none of the characters feel developed at all, and the crime thriller aspect doesn’t gel well with the feel-good story. At least there are some beautiful sequences that make drifting a car feel like an artform.

articles.title: Hollywood producer spent 25 years praying for Tinseltown, says 'you can't hate them'
articles.summary: Faith-based Hollywood Prayer Network celebrates 25 years of praying and creating community for entertainment’s storytellers.
articles.body: Hollywood is a place many Christians have condemned; Karen Covell has spent 25 years asking them to pray for the people who work there instead. She is the founder of the Hollywood Prayer Network and sees the town as her greatest ministry. After all, screenwriters themselves have long preached the maxim "story is everything," and if stories create meaning, influence emotions and shape identity, then Hollywood is the most influential mission field there ever was. That’s what Covell was thinking when she began the faith-based organization that, along with her staff and now 170+ chapters in 42 countries, just celebrated its 25th anniversary with a Gatsby-themed gala in downtown Los Angeles. FORMER DISNEY STAR DAVID HENRIE REJECTED 'SECULAR' HOLLYWOOD LIFESTYLE AFTER LIFE-CHANGING MONASTERY VISIT Founded in 2001, the Hollywood Prayer Network, through prayer, community and resources, supports the entertainment industry’s storytellers and believes the next generation of actors, writers, directors and producers doesn't have to maneuver Tinseltown alone. The organization offers everything from intercessory prayer and professional discipleship programs to networking and Bible studies. "We have a beautiful community here. You couldn't get me out of this place for anything because the people that are here are wonderful," Covell told Fox News Digital. It was more than 25 years ago that Covell, along with her composer husband, Jim Covell, saw and felt the need for believers in Hollywood to have support. KEVIN SORBO BLASTS HOLLYWOOD 'BLACKLISTING' OF CONSERVATIVES AS 'SEVENTH GRADE MEAN GIRLS' CULTURE "It's competitive, a lot of people look for work, we're all freelancers, and we wanted to support the people of faith here who really felt like they had one foot in the church and one foot in the Hollywood entertainment industry and neither one liked each other," Covell, who originally came to Los Angeles to attend the University of Southern California, explained. While the two had already started a prayer group, they found that those coming to Los Angeles out of the church arrived in the city, as she put it, already "beat up." SKILLET’S JOHN COOPER SAYS CHRISTIANS WHO CALL ROCK MUSIC ‘DEMONIC’ ARE ‘GETTING THE GOSPEL WRONG’ "I knew Hollywood didn't like the church because we were really terrible to them — we boycotted, we threw out our TVs, we burned their books — we wouldn't go to their movies, you know, but I believed if you pray for somebody, you can't hate them," Covell said. She recalled hearing stories from people in the group whose families, pastors and friends had warned them not to go to Los Angeles — that it was Satan's pit and that they couldn't live there. HOLLYWOOD PRODUCER BEHIND 'APOLLO 13' REJECTS POLITICS IN HIS MOVIES, SEEKS TO UNITE AUDIENCES "And I said, ‘This is ridiculous. We should be storytellers, we should be creative. God created us to be creative.’" So Covell decided to try to figure out a way to build a bridge between the church in America and Hollywood. NEARLY 500 PUBLIC FIGURES FROM POLITICS TO HOLLYWOOD WILL READ BIBLE COVER TO COVER TO MARK AMERICA'S 250TH "I thought, ‘I've got to get the church to start understanding the beauty and the importance of Hollywood,’" she said. Since then, whether someone is a believer or not, the HPN has prayed for people ranging from fledgling singers to the likes of Britney Spears during her periods of intense tabloid scrutiny and personal struggle. Paris Hilton has received intercessory prayer while Robert Downey Jr. was lifted up during his public battle with addiction. There have been many prayers for wildlife, crisis relief efforts and, recently, for celebrity blogger Perez Hilton following his distressing livestream and subsequent hospitalization. NEW STUDY REVEALS THE SINGLE MOST CRITICAL FACTOR IN WHETHER CHILDREN KEEP THEIR FAITH INTO ADULTHOOD Through its monthly Kids Prayer Calendar, "Ones2Watch," members support child and teen actors in prayer before they face major industry pressures. The organization has established numerous community groups geared toward directors, dancers, writers, comedians and people working in technology and AI. It has local chapters across the United States, each serving entertainment professionals through mentorship, networking and worship. It also has its own app, which lists its resources, local chapters around the world and community events. "We have gatherings of people all over the city and all over the country and the world who say, yes, it's important to be storytellers," Covell said, noting that she has found what really attacks artists is isolation, discouragement and fear. "Those three things can all be combated in community." For her part, Covell credits her 42-year marriage to a husband who counts the days they’ve been together as a big part of her own success. The two, who recently finished a book titled "Confessions of a Hollywood Marriage," as she put it, "pray together every day and walk with each other through the hard and good times." "It's not a how-to book, it's not anything to help people, it is just us telling the story of our marriage and how it's been such a beautiful and amazing journey for the last 42 years," Covell said. "It's not because we're any different or special… We know people see so many bad marriages that they lose hope that it's possible. And we just let people know, this is the greatest gift." Just last year, Covell chose to step down from producing and instead devote herself fully to the Hollywood Prayer Network, which she said has been growing quickly of late. It wasn’t that way at the start. "I take credit for having, I think, the slowest-growing ministry on the planet. It was just one person at a time. Would you pray for Hollywood?" Covell quipped. "And I just kept going." Recently, staff and members posted a video on the organization’s social media showing Covell jokingly preparing for a "Netflix documentary" about what it’s like to be a Christian in Hollywood. The viral posts included disclaimers clarifying that the Netflix part was just a ruse based on a popular online video trend. Covell just wants to keep supporting storytellers as they tell great stories and reminding them that they’re not alone in the process. "… As a producer, I worked in Hollywood and in the secular industry. My husband is still writing music in the secular industry. We love the commercial industry of Hollywood. We love the people, we love the projects, we love the place," she said. "This ministry started growing and I slowly started seeing other people come with the same feeling of, ‘Well, let's build community. Let's be together. Let's love the people we're here with. Let's celebrate being storytellers.’" CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "We want to tell great stories that inspire people, that encourage people. And we want to know that we're not alone doing it. So, that's my purpose with the prayer network."

articles.title: ‘Family Affair’ star Kathy Garver says failed remake ‘sucked,’ reveals what went wrong
articles.summary: Kathy Garver called the 2002 "Family Affair" remake terrible, saying Gary Cole and Tim Curry couldn't replicate the original cast's deep warmth.
articles.body: Kathy Garver is not holding back about the failed 2002 remake of "Family Affair." In a new interview with Fox News Digital, Garver — who is gearing up to celebrate the 60th anniversary of "Family Affair" by hosting a special marathon featured on Catchy Comedy — explained why the reboot lacked the chemistry, warmth and familial bond that made the classic show so beloved. "Excuse my language, but it sucked," Garver, who portrayed Cissy in the original series, said. "And it did for many reasons." 'FAMILY AFFAIR' STAR TALKS 'SURVIVING CISSY,' SEEING ANISSA JONES FOR THE LAST TIME AND ALLEGED SITCOM CURSE The original "Family Affair" premiered in 1966 and followed bachelor Bill Davis as he unexpectedly became the guardian of his late brother and sister-in-law's three children: Cissy, Buffy and Jody. Brian Keith played Bill, while Sebastian Cabot portrayed the family’s butler, Mr. French. The 2002 remake featured Gary Cole as Bill Davis and Tim Curry as Mr. French. Although Garver praised both actors, she said they brought entirely different qualities to the characters audiences had already grown attached to. KELSEY GRAMMER ADMITS IT'S 'EXHAUSTING' WHEN MOVIES TRY TO ALTER HISTORY TO FIT MODERN TASTES "I think it’s very difficult to do a remake," Garver said. "When they see Gary Cole, they say, ‘Well, that’s not Uncle Bill.’" Cole was "great in ‘NCIS,’" Garver said, but "as you know, he’s no Brian Keith." Keith’s appeal, she explained, came from the contrast between his tough exterior and his tenderness toward the children. GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Brian Keith was "this macho guy, the ex-Marine," Garver said. "And here he is, this loving dad." TIM CURRY'S CAUSE OF DEATH REVEALED Garver also felt Curry’s portrayal of Mr. French was too far removed from Cabot’s understated performance. "Tim Curry had a whole different take on it," she said. "It was very good, but it wasn’t in a situation-comedy vein. It was like the Tim Curry show." "And so that didn’t quite mesh with Sebastian Cabot, who was a wonderful actor," she added. Garver described Curry’s Mr. French as "loud and boisterous," while Cabot’s version was "much more low-key." ORIGINAL 'LITTLE HOUSE' VILLAIN RETURNS FOR REBOOT WITH WARNING FOR NEW NELLIE Cabot’s performance was also rooted in his character’s love for the children, Garver said — something she felt the remake failed to convey. "He, too, did everything in love," she said. "And basically, he loved the children. And I think that was missing from Tim Curry." WATCH: ‘FAMILY AFFAIR’ STAR KATHY GARVER SAYS FAILED REMAKE ‘SUCKED,’ REVEALS WHAT WENT WRONG The actress said the original cast members brought an authentic sense of family to the show because their characters genuinely cared for one another. "Each individual person on the original ‘Family Affair’ had a family that they loved," Garver said. ‘BRADY BUNCH’ CAST MADE NEARLY NOTHING FROM DECADES OF RERUNS, EVE PLUMB CLAIMS Garver credited that emotional connection with helping the show stand out from other sitcoms of its era. "I think it was a groundbreaker," she said. "It was the first of its kind — a single father, or a single uncle, single relative, that all of a sudden gets three orphan children." The series also benefited from its production quality, according to Garver. She noted that "Family Affair" was among the early television sitcoms filmed in color and that many of the cast and crew members came from the movie industry. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "So it was a real quality kind of show," she said. Garver said the original series also featured "relatable characters" and storylines that continue to resonate with audiences. "It has stories that endure today," she said. "And so it remains relatable, I believe, because it’s a family. And how — what do I do with the family? How do I deal with these problems? And it shows you that." She also believed the warmth of the original series was reflected in the way the characters interacted with one another. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "People really like each other — what a concept," Garver said. "People aren’t yelling and screaming at them. You have this very calm person that’s listening to you." Garver said the original cast’s chemistry was also visible in their performances. "Our creator, Ed Hartman, who was just a fabulous writer, creator and producer, told me, ‘Kathy, it’s in the eyes. You act through your eyes. What is coming through them?’" "I think that warmth is something that’s sustained," she added. For Garver, the enduring appeal of "Family Affair" comes down to the emotional comfort it continues to provide viewers. She described the show as "a comfort" and compared watching it to "taking a bite of the comfort cake." "It’s not all this chaos, but something that’s beautiful and lovely and watchable," Garver said. articles.title: Former Bond girl says next 007 should be 'another gorgeous man' as James Bond decision
articles.summary: Alison Papworth weighed in on who should play James Bond in the iconic film franchise. The actress appeared in "For Your Eyes Only" and "Octopussy."
articles.body: The search for the next 007 is underway, and former Bond girl Alison Papworth has a clear message: leave one thing untouched. "What do I hope? I know they’re about to announce the next Bond, aren’t they?" the actress, who also works as a director for a London-based design and consultancy firm, told Fox News Digital. "And we’re all waiting with bated breath." "If they’re true to the books, I hope it’s a man," she said. "A man, just a man. Yes, I think it would be very strange if it were a woman. Don’t you? It would be a totally different thing. So I hope it’s another man, another gorgeous man." AMAZON ANNOUNCES SEARCH FOR NEXT JAMES BOND IS UNDERWAY, AS HOLLYWOOD CASTING CHOICES COME UNDER SCRUTINY Papworth’s comments came before Gary Oldman said on "The Morning Show" that his "Slow Horses" costar Jack Lowden could be the next James Bond. "Jack, it’s been rumored that he’s on the shortlist," Oldman said on the Canadian talk show. "We’re going to find out pretty soon, aren’t we? Because they have picked him. They have made their choice, but they have not announced it yet. So my fingers are crossed for Jack." According to Deadline, Oldman later clarified his comments, saying: "There’s six people on a shortlist. I heard a rumor that they’ve picked James Bond, but they haven’t announced it yet, which is their prerogative. So I do not know [who has got the part], but I’m hoping it’s Jack." Amazon MGM Studios gained creative control of the James Bond franchise in 2025 after forming a joint venture with longtime Bond producers Michael G. Wilson and Barbara Broccoli. WATCH: BOND GIRL ALISON PAPWORTH REVEALS HER HOPE FOR THE NEXT 007 In May, the studio announced that the search for the next James Bond was underway. Denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next installment, with Steven Knight writing the screenplay. Daniel Craig last played 007 in 2021's "No Time to Die." People magazine reported that Paul Mescal, Jacob Elordi and Jack O'Connell are among the actors rumored to be in the running to take over the iconic role. The upcoming release will be the 26th Bond film in the more than 60-year-old franchise. Papworth appeared in 1981’s "For Your Eyes Only" and 1983’s "Octopussy," both of which starred Roger Moore. "He was an absolute gentleman," she said. "Yes, I know everybody says it. I only have fabulous, fabulous memories of him being funny, telling the best jokes. Very dry, very droll." "One thing I really remember about him, when we were in India, there was a stuntman, I think it was a stuntman. He used to smuggle beef drippings in his luggage for Roger because he loved it. It was very funny, and it stuck in my mind all those years later." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Being a Bond girl had its benefits. Papworth recalled being flown first class to Rio de Janeiro, where vodka was flowing for the cast, and she tried caviar for the first time. In between filming, she would observe Moore playing Backgammon at picture-worthy destinations. But life on set wasn't always as luxurious. "It was the middle of winter doing the scenes for 'Octopussy' where we were fighting in the castle," Papworth recalled. "We learned to stunt fight, and it was supposed to be in India. But we were at Pinewood Studios, and it was below freezing. All the girls had these red bodysuits on with big capes. We were so cold, we had thermals on underneath, so we probably looked about five pounds heavier." Papworth didn’t expect to appear in two Bond films. She recalled a publicity director once telling her, "Once you’ve done a Bond movie, you get thrown on the Bond Girl scrap heap." But Broccoli, daughter of longtime Bond producer Albert "Cubby" Broccoli, had a different idea. "You can imagine my surprise when I got the call from Barbara Broccoli saying, 'You’re on the next one, Alison,'" she said. "And it stayed with me. Bond has stayed with me. It’s changed my life. My two best friends, I met one on 'For Your Eyes Only,' Vanya Seager; she was another Bond girl. And I met my other best friend, Carole Ashby, on 'Octopussy.' Carol was there when my baby was born. Vanya and I, we speak every day. I speak to them both every day." "So without Bond, I wouldn’t have those two incredible bonds," she added. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS After appearing in two Bond movies, Papworth continued acting and modeling. By the time she reached her 30s, however, her modeling career was "leveling out." "My husband had lots of properties, and I’d always loved interior design," she said. "I’m totally self-taught, but I’m passionate about it. And he just started giving me properties to do, and that developed into our business, which has been running successfully for all these years. I still love it. And after he died, I carried on. He taught me well." Today, Papworth is a director at Camhall Design & Consultancy, an interior design company based in the U.K. It has completed projects in London, New York, Boston and the Bahamas. She also helped launch Lustre & Lustre London, which offers "luxury cleaning services." Papworth and her close pal, Joan Collins, also teamed up to raise funds for Shooting Star Children's Hospices. According to the organization's site, it supports, "babies, children and young people with life-limiting conditions, and their families, across south-west London, north-west London and Surrey." Papworth still has fond memories of her time bringing the Bond stories to life. PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE "I love show business," she said. "I really do. It’s fabulous. And maybe I’m lucky that I’m not super famous, so I can have a private life. I’m not like my dear friend Joan who gets stopped everywhere. I’m lucky because I can dip in and out of it." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I still do signings," Papworth continued. "It went quiet through my 30s and 40s. And then, I don’t know. Bond fans are very good at tracking you down. I started to get invites to do signings. I remember doing my first signing in Birmingham at this huge exhibition center. My husband and my kids came because I was a first-time signer. There were all 'Star Wars,' 'Doctor Who,' astronauts, boxers, and little me."

Meghan Markle has shared a first look at her family's return to the U.K.

In a Sunday, Sept. 13, Instagram post , the Duchess of Sussex, 45, shared a video highlighting life in England after she and husband Prince Harry recently returned with their children, son Prince Archie , 7, and daughter Princess Lilibet , 5, and their dogs , Pula and Mia.

At the start of the 35-second clip, Meghan and Harry, 41, can be seen walking hand in hand outdoors, before the video transitions to scenes of what appear to be Lilibet's feet before a fireplace and Meghan splashing around in a muddy puddle.

The video then shows Lilibet riding a bicycle, as Archie — with a British accent — cheers her on, exclaiming, "Go! Go!" before running beside her. Wham 's "Wake Me Up Before You Go-Go" then starts to play, as more outdoorsy recordings, including Harry, Archie and Lilibet fishing on a boat, are featured.

Throughout the entire video, two emojis are placed at the top: one of a British flag and another of a red heart.

Meghan and Harry arrived in the U.K. on Aug. 26, just a week after PEOPLE revealed that they were relocating to Harry's home country with their family for an extended period.

A source told PEOPLE that the Duke and Duchess of Sussex spent their last weekend before their move to the U.K. with close friends, including those of their children and Meghan's mom, Doria Ragland .

Following the move, a source close to Harry and Meghan told PEOPLE that settling the children "has been, and remains, their focus."

"Everything else will fall into place when the time is right," the insider continued. "There is a lot to do. They have just moved halfway across the world, and it's been really busy getting the kids settled. Their focus has been on that, and will remain on that, for the time being. They are happy to be back."

Harry and Meghan's family plan to make a private, non-royal residence in the U.K. their home base for an extended period, with Archie and Lilibet attending school in Britain. They will also maintain their home in California and vacation property in Portugal.

The couple is also not returning to royal roles . articles.title: Celine Dion makes triumphant return in Paris after six years sidelined by rare diagnosis
articles.summary: PARIS — It’s all coming back to her now.
articles.body: PARIS — It’s all coming back to her now. If there were any doubts about whether the “Queen of Ballads” could still hit the high notes, they were put to rest on Saturday night when she belted out “All by Myself,” one of her most difficult songs, in front of 30,000 adoring fans in Paris. It was a poignant comeback for the Quebec-born singer, 58, who was forced to stop touring six years ago after being diagnosed with a rare neurological disorder, stiff-person syndrome. Having spent the years since largely out of the spotlight, Dion was overcome with emotion, breaking down in tears during the first few minutes of her show at Plenitude Arena, one of Europe’s largest indoor concert venues. Aptly, she began with the French-language song “On ne change pas” — which translates to “one doesn’t change” — an apparent signal that she is the same Celine as ever. The road to recovery has been “rocky and longer than it should have been,” she told the crowd, after she endured years of physical therapy and medical treatments. There were nerves mixed with raw emotion as she asked the crowd: “Can you hear my heartbeat?” Dion, an icon across the French-speaking world, spoke of fulfilling her “promise” to come back. Two years ago, she sang here from the Eiffel Tower during the 2024 Olympics opening ceremony, marking a milestone in her recovery in front of a TV audience of hundreds of millions. Despite living with an illness that at times prevents her from singing or even walking due to severe muscle spasms, Dion on Saturday mixed classic onstage theatrics with titanic ballads for more than two hours. The concert, the first in a two-part, 26-show residency in the city, was hotly anticipated, with 9 million people entering a presale ticket lottery back in April. Some American fans told NBC News they paid $1,200 per ticket on the resale market. After the show, fans emerged in disbelief. “It was a victory lap,” said Francesca Pezzulo, 31, from Los Angeles. “I think her belief is renewed, I think her spirit is renewed.” It was a bucket-list moment for Ashley Hammond, 42, who flew in from Miami for the concert. “It gave you chills. It was everything we dreamed of,” she said. Fans came from all corners of the world for the moment. “I think Celine is the queen,” Pirkir Gutlausson, a 53-year-old mechanic from Iceland, told NBC News. Dion is performing a total of 16 concerts until October, with a further 10 in the spring of 2027. The residency is expected to cause a mini tourism boom, with an influx of hundreds of thousands of fans spending millions of dollars on par with Taylor Swift’s shows in Paris, according to the hospitality and tourism consultancy MKG. For eager fans, there were plenty of opportunities to spend money. A Celine pop-up store at fashion boutique Galeries Lafayette had some T-shirts on sale for $145. The luxurious hotel Le Royal Monceau has been the focal point of Celine mania. Since her arrival in the French capital, a constant stream of fans has waited day and night for a chance to see the global superstar, who has often stopped to sing and dance along with the crowds, even when returning from rehearsals in the middle of the night. For fans, her resilience says it all. “She has class, she’s humane and she’s a fighter,” said Karine Teixeira Bourgogne, 58, who traveled from across France to see her.

Hollywood star Catherine Zeta-Jones has declared the phrase "nepo baby" is "horrific", saying: "These kids didn't ask to be born into this."

The term refers to children of famous parents perceived to have achieved riches and success off their parents' backs.

The 56-year-old actress, married to Kirk Douglas' son Michael Douglas, has two children - Dylan and Carys - who have both followed their parents into showbiz.

Dylan, she said, was pursuing acting while Carys was interested in directing. She told The Sunday Times they were "plugging away".

"You have to go with your dreams, your passion," Zeta-Jones said.

"It's hard for them to forge a way forward on their own.

"This horrific phrase 'nepo baby' is horrible because these kids didn't ask to be born into this, they're finding their own way in life.

"Otherwise, Michael and I would be the first to go, 'you know what? Maybe law school looks really good'."

Zeta-Jones' big break came when she landed a West End role in 42nd Street in 1987, becoming a household name in the UK in 1991 when she starred in ITV hit The Darling Buds Of May with Only Fools and Horses legend David Jason.

She has since become a global superstar, with roles in The Mask Of Zorro, Entrapment, Traffic and 2002's adaptation of Chicago.

"I had a sniff of the joy of being in the theatre so young," she said.

"I went, 'I want to do this. I can't imagine going through school and A-Levels in Swansea.'"

Zeta-Jones met Romancing The Stone star Douglas, 81, at France's Deauville Film Festival, in August 1998.

With a 25-year age gap between them, they were engaged a year later, marrying at The Plaza hotel in New York in 2000.

Dylan was born in 2000 and Carys in 2003.

articles.title: Viral video shows bystanders warning elderly man who has no clue he's being followed by a huge black bear
articles.summary: Video with over 35 million views captures a black bear silently following an elderly man down a British Columbia sidewalk before bystanders intervene.
articles.body: An elderly man had what has been labeled a "close call" with a black bear, although he wasn’t initially aware of the fact that a bear was following him as he shuffled down the sidewalk. Not until it was pointed out to him. The video of the man, the bear, and the bystanders pointing out that he's being followed was posted on Instagram by Quail guy. It has more than 35 million views and when you see how close the bear is to the man you understand why. The man, reportedly in British Columbia, is shuffling along on a sidewalk holding a bag minding his own business. He walks by a black bear seemingly not even noticing that it's just feet from him. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS Bystanders across the street try to warn him that the rather large bear is behind him and appears to be following him. After he realizes what they're saying, the man turns and looks at the bear, then picks up the pace as he continues walking. And by picking up the pace, I mean he goes from almost standing still to actually standing still before taking off, probably as fast as he can shuffle his feet. 6 OF THE BEST FALL CAMPING DESTINATIONS IN AMERICA, PLUS GEAR BEGINNERS SHOULD PACK The concerned group of bystanders did what they set out to do. They warned the man. They were loud enough to get the bear to turn around, and they didn’t step foot off of the sidewalk from across the street. Another potential disaster avoided. The old man presumably made it the rest of the way home without unknowingly wandering into another close call with nature or anything else. PIZZA DELIVERY MAN DESERVES A RAISE AFTER WALKING PAST A BLACK BEAR TO DELIVER CUSTOMER'S ORDER Just as important was someone documenting it all on video. You hope for the best in that type of situation, but if it does go sideways, you have some game film to study and learn from.

articles.body: As global leaders gather in New Delhi for the 18th BRICS Summit, India is in the spotlight as the host of the two-day event at Bharat Mandapam which began from September 12 to 13. With discussions ranging from geopolitics and economic cooperation to intra-BRICS trade, infrastructure and sustainable development, the summit has brought together representatives of some of the world's major emerging economies.BRICS, which now comprises 11 major emerging and developing countries, began as a much smaller grouping. The term BRIC was coined by economist Jim O'Neill in 2001 to describe Brazil, Russia, India and China. The four countries began their informal dialogue in 2006, before Russia hosted the first BRIC summit in 2009. South Africa joined in 2010, followed by Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, Saudi Arabia and the UAE in 2024. Indonesia became a member in 2025, when partner countries were also brought into the framework.With the summit putting the spotlight on the BRICS nations, here's a look at some Indian celebrities who have reportedly invested in properties in countries that are part of the grouping.Shah Rukh KhanShah Rukh Khan has an impressive property portfolio in India, with his iconic Mumbai residence Mannat reportedly valued at around Rs 300 crore. The beachfront property, reportedly named Jannat, is said to be worth around Rs 100 crore.Aishwarya Rai and Abhishek BachchanAishwarya Rai and Abhishek Bachchan reside with Amitabh Bachchan and Jaya Bachchan at Jalsa, the family's 10,125 sq ft bungalow in Mumbai.The couple also owns a 5-BHK apartment in Bandra-Kurla Complex (BKC), reportedly purchased for Rs 21 crore, along with a property on the 37th floor of Skylark Tower in Worli.Their international property portfolio includes a lavish mansion at Jumeirah Golf Estates in Dubai, which reportedly cost around Rs 16 crore.R MadhavanR Madhavan is also known to have invested in properties in different Indian cities. articles.title: The Units’ Digital Stimulation is synthpunk perfection
articles.summary: The 1980 record Digital Stimulation from the San Francisco synthpunk band The Units is raw, infectious, and shockingly modern.
articles.body: The Units are a band I discovered in part thanks to No Dogs in Space. During their miniseries on The Screamers (another incredible band worth checking out), they mention synthpunk.org as one of their sources. And there’s no better way to get my attention than to combine two of my favorite things — punk rock and synthesizers. The site was down that day (it appears to be back up now), but I was able to access a version from July through the Wayback Machine. What greeted me was a bare-bones site with links for six bands, including The Screamers. But at the top was The Units, a band I’d never heard of and, after tracking down their 1980 record Digital Stimulation, I fell in love. [Media: The production, especially on the Devo-esque vocals, feels distinctly of its time. But the sound palette and arrangements are more aggressive, dancier, and generally just more modern-sounding. Ignoring the vocals, album opener “High Pressure” could pass as an MSPAINT song. The title track, with its sped-up disco stomp, could have been released by DFA in 2003. And many of the later tracks would be at home on a Single Frame record. The Units weren’t the first punk band to dabble with synths. Nor were they the first act to largely replace guitars with keyboards and lean into technology as a core theme of their songwriting. The Talking Heads offered a cleaner, artier take on punk, incorporating keyboards, non-Western percussion, and even tape loops. Devo’s first single, “Mongoloid,” has a distinctly punk edge that would have been right at home alongside The Units. But the band still leaned heavily on traditional guitar and bass, and always felt more at home in the art-rock and new wave scenes. Husband-and-wife duo Scott Ryser and Rachel Webber, the primary songwriters of The Units, had a sharper edge to their sound. They were firmly grounded in the West Coast punk scene that made its DIY ethos a core part of its identity. Their contemporaries were the Dead Kennedys, The Mutants, and The Avengers. You can hear it in the lean arrangements that prioritize raw energy over perfection. That’s not to say songs like “Cannibals” and “Bugboy” are simplistic. Their bleak, slightly humorous critiques of an uncaring world are models of efficiency — unfussy and infectious. Like a lot of Bay Area punk bands, there’s a melodicism to The Units’ work that is hard to shake. “Warm Moving Bodies” feels like a dancefloor anthem waiting to happen, and “High Pressure” is an undeniable earworm. The band did record a second album in 1981, Animals They Dream About, but it remained unreleased until 2016. It’s also an excellent document of the under-represented synthpunk scene of the late ‘70s and early ‘80s. Though, it is far more polished and leans into poppier new wave arrangements that are a step removed from their bootstrapped punk roots. The Units’ Digital Stimulation is available on Bandcamp and via streaming on Apple Music, YouTube Music, and Deezer.

articles.title: Joanna Gaines reveals why she and Chip walked away from 'Fixer Upper' at the height of its success
articles.summary: Joanna Gaines described a deep "soul weariness" that led her and Chip Gaines to walk away from "Fixer Upper" despite pressure to keep going.
articles.body: Joanna Gaines had success knocking on every door — and she decided to stop answering. At the height of "Fixer Upper" fame, the home design and lifestyle expert and her husband, Chip Gaines, walked away from the nonstop grind despite pressure from their representatives to keep going. Years later, Joanna explained that she had reached a point where she was experiencing what she called "soul weariness." JOANNA GAINES KEEPS LIFE SIMPLE IN TEXAS AWAY FROM HOLLYWOOD SPOTLIGHT "When you start realizing you're living on a thing that's now… the intentionality is gone, and you're just showing up… that doesn't feel fulfilling," she said on the "Joy 101 with Hoda Kotb" podcast. "It actually feels as though we're part of this machine that is like, 'What's the life here?'" She added, "I would say that was our first pause of like, ‘We're doing all this and seeing great reward … this is wonderful,’ but also never at the expense of … our like livelihood, our happiness, our souls." That pause would become a blueprint for how Joanna thinks about work — and burnout — today. "Stopping in that moment was basically us saying … ‘What's worth it is, like are we healthy? Are we good? Is our family good?’ That's the most important thing. So that was really a very pivotal moment for us." "Fixer Upper" turned Chip and Joanna into television stars, but even as the HGTV hit reached new heights, the couple knew they couldn't keep running at full speed forever. The Gaines’s first stepped in front of television cameras when the "Fixer Upper" pilot aired in 2013. The series followed the husband-and-wife duo as they took on rundown homes in Waco, Texas, and transformed them into polished spaces for their clients — all while growing their increasingly influential Magnolia brand. The show quickly became a hit, making Joanna and Chip familiar faces far beyond the world of home renovation. COUNTRY STAR STEPS AWAY FROM MUSIC TO FOCUS ON HIMSELF AFTER FAME TOOK A TOLL In September 2017, the couple announced they would end "Fixer Upper" after its fifth season, choosing to step away while the series was still riding high. Joanna said she and Chip have spent almost 25 years building their business. But about three years ago, she said, they stopped seeing where they were headed. "We stopped seeing vision. We stopped remembering, ‘Like why are we doing this?’" The couple decided to take the summer off. KATHIE LEE GIFFORD ADMITS SHE 'WANTED TO DIE' AFTER MISDIAGNOSIS AND MULTIPLE SURGERIES FOR CHRONIC PAIN However, the decision wasn't consequence-free. Joanna acknowledged that stepping away meant putting pressure on their team. "Which meant disappointing our team, disappointing a lot of things … So it cost us something. It cost people something." "But that three months was time for us to go, ‘We need a break. We need clarity. Why are we building this? What are we doing this for?’" Joanna remembered the moment she felt the burnout was impossible to ignore. "When you start dreading your days, like ‘I don't want to do that.’" For Gaines, that sense of dread eventually became so pronounced that she found herself looking for almost any excuse to hit pause — even an unexpected illness. "You start like wishing for a stomach bug or … 'Okay, maybe back surgery this year would be great.’ Like how do I force myself?" she laughed. '80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD Physical exhaustion, Joanna explained, is something she knows how to push through. But the deeper exhaustion is different, she argued. "So there's that part, but also just … where your soul just feels weary." She described the "soul" as the deeper part of a person — the place that can run dry even when the body is still capable of performing. LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS "From a physical standpoint, I can work till I can … I can push past the weariness the physical, but then you get to that layer of like the soul weariness and that's dangerous." Joanna said that was the warning she is now determined not to ignore, describing the feeling as a "holy fear." For the entrepreneur and television personality who built an empire by constantly creating, the hardest lesson may have been learning that she cannot simply outwork exhaustion. The Magnolia Network stars tied the knot in 2003. Joanna and Chip are parents to five children — Ella, Drake, Crew, Emmie and Duke.
